subject: Seven rupees more, forty-three on his back
alt: Rakesh Ranjan's cartoon: slanting lines split the frame in two. In the left half stands Narendra Modi - saffron vest, white dhoti, white beard - and his speech bubble says: diesel had to be made 50 rupees a litre costlier .... Inside that half, in a slanting strip, the same Modi stands upside down on one hand, holding a mace whose ball rests on the ground, and his bubble says: raised only 7 rupees. In the right half a bearded labourer with a green band on his head stands bent at the waist; Modi stands on his back, lifting a large brown bundle above his head with both hands. The shaft of the mace rests on the labourer's shoulder with its ball on the ground; he is sweating, and two marks of alarm stand above him. Modi's bubble says: the government lifted the burden of 43 rupees! The cartoonist's signature, RAKESH RANJAN, is at the lower right.
chutki: On 12 November, at the Kisan Tak Bharat conference, the prime minister said that with crude oil climbing from 70 to 122 dollars a barrel, diesel would have had to cost 50 rupees a litre more; the government raised the price by only 7 and carried the other 43 itself. Ranjan turns that arithmetic into a picture: the burden is held up high, but its weight sits on the waist of the man bent below.

The needle is on the man who does not appear in the official statement. The one announcing the saving of 43 rupees stands on his head, mace in hand; the one actually hauling the load on his back is the labourer. The farmer and worker in whose name the claim is made are placed at the very bottom of the picture.
